titre: A Businessman Lost on a Battlefield
accroche: In 1859, a man from Geneva on a business trip comes upon forty thousand abandoned wounded. Five years later, twelve states sign a treaty.
contenu_vulgarise:
On June 24, 1859, a Geneva businessman named Henry Dunant arrives in northern Italy. He is trying to meet Napoleon III about an agricultural concession in Algeria. He reaches Solferino on the very evening of the battle, one of the deadliest of the century. Forty thousand men lie on the field, dead, dying or wounded, and almost no one is tending to them. The armies' medical services are pitiful compared with the numbers.

Dunant drops his business, stays several days, and organizes the inhabitants of the nearby villages to bring relief. He has the wounded treated without regard to uniform, and a phrase then spreads among the women of Castiglione: *tutti fratelli*, all brothers.

## The Book, and the Two Ideas It Contains

Back in Geneva, Dunant writes *Un souvenir de Solférino* (A Memory of Solferino), which he publishes at his own expense in 1862, in sixteen hundred copies. The account is precise and unbearable, but what matters most is in the last pages, where he makes two proposals.

The first: set up, in every country and in peacetime, voluntary relief societies ready to step in when war comes. The second, more legal: have states adopt an international principle that would protect this relief work and make it inviolable on the battlefield.

What follows is swift. On February 9, 1863, the Geneva Society for Public Welfare looks favorably on the book and appoints a commission of five people, Dunant among them. Its first meeting, on February 17, 1863, is now regarded as the founding date of the International Committee of the Red Cross. A year and a half later, a diplomatic conference called by the Swiss government leads to the first Geneva Convention, signed on August 22, 1864 by twelve states.

## What This Treaty Does to the Law of War

The law of war existed before 1864, but it governed relations between belligerents: what one state owes another state. The Geneva Convention introduces something else. It makes ambulances, military hospitals and the personnel who serve in them neutral, whichever side they belong to, and requires that the wounded be collected and cared for without regard to nationality.

In other words, it creates a category of people who cease to be enemies. The wounded man is no longer a combatant temporarily out of action; he is a protected person, and caring for him no longer depends on an agreement between the two sides but on a commitment made to everyone.

From this shift comes all of modern international humanitarian law, including its most counterintuitive principle: certain rules bind even the party that is in the right, even against the party that is in the wrong, and even when the adversary does not respect them.

repere.texte: Five years separate the Battle of Solferino, on June 24, 1859, from the first Geneva Convention, signed on August 22, 1864 by twelve states.
repere.source: Geneva Convention of August 22, 1864, signed by twelve European states; Article 1 on the neutrality of ambulances and military hospitals

carte.punch: The wounded man stops being an enemy. A treaty from 1864 creates that category.
carte.idee: Henry Dunant arrives at Solferino on the evening of the 1859 battle: forty thousand men dead, dying or wounded, almost without help. His 1862 book proposes an international principle. In 1864, twelve states sign the first Geneva Convention, which makes ambulances neutral.

quiz.question: What does the 1864 Geneva Convention introduce that the earlier law of war did not provide for?
choix: A ban on armies using certain categories of weapons judged too deadly
An obligation for belligerents to declare war before opening hostilities
The neutrality of ambulances and their personnel, and the duty to care for the wounded regardless of side
The creation of an international court with jurisdiction over crimes committed in the field
quiz.explication: Until then, the law of war governed relations between belligerent states. The Convention makes ambulances, military hospitals and those who serve in them neutral, and requires that the wounded be cared for whatever their nationality, thereby creating a category of people who cease to be enemies.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why is Henry Dunant in northern Italy in June 1859?
choix: He is trying to meet Napoleon III about an agricultural concession in Algeria
He is accompanying the French army's general staff as a press correspondent
He is fleeing Geneva after a financial dispute with business partners
He has been sent by the Geneva Society for Public Welfare to observe the battle
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Dunant is a businessman who came to find Napoleon III about an agricultural concession in Algeria, not a press correspondent or an envoy of the Geneva Society, whose interest in his project he would only see on his return.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What do the last pages of *Un souvenir de Solférino*, the book Dunant published in 1862, propose?
choix: The creation of an international army to separate the belligerents
The establishment of an annual public holiday in memory of the victims of Solferino
Voluntary relief societies in each country and an international principle protecting relief work
Payment by states of compensation to the families of soldiers killed in combat
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Dunant makes two proposals: voluntary relief societies set up in peacetime in each country, and an international principle that would make this relief work inviolable on the battlefield.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which date is now regarded as the founding date of the International Committee of the Red Cross?
choix: June 24, 1859, the day of the Battle of Solferino
February 17, 1863, the date of the first meeting of the five-member commission
August 22, 1864, the day the Geneva Convention was signed
February 9, 1863, the day the Geneva Society examined Dunant's book
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The commission of five people, Dunant among them, appointed on February 9, 1863, holds its first meeting on February 17, 1863: that is the date now regarded as the founding of the ICRC, distinct from the battle and the treaty.
